newsitem.title: UK: European shares rally, dlr rebounds vs mark.
newsitem.headline: European shares rally, dlr rebounds vs mark.

text.p: European shares rallied after opening weaker on Tuesday and by midday the London and Frankfurt bourses were modestly higher, although French shares were still down on doubts over France's stance on European economic and monetary union (EMU).
By midday, France's blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 19.47 points, or 0.7 percent, at 2,666.73, having been down over one percent earlier.
The market had extended Monday's steep fall on concerns over the euro and France's wrangling about the stability pact designed to ensure budgetary discipline under EMU.
"There are no buyers around, there's no support for the market," said a French broker earlier.
The London share market was up 0.2 percent at 1130 GMT however, and the Frankfurt bourse was up 0.04 percent.
Wall Street's latest surge, which saw the Dow Jones Industrial Average of leading U.S. stocks rise another 42.72 points overnight to its second record in a row, offered background support.
The Dow has surged more than 1,000 points since the start of 1997 and is now benefiting from the dollar's recent weakness which is boosting shares in big U.S. exporting companies.

The latest bout of worries over EMU surfaced on Monday when French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn and other European Union officials said a delay in approving the stability pact was not a precursor to renegotiating it.

But traders will remain jittery about the outlook for EMU until France gives its verdict on the stability pact. French European Affairs Minister Pierre Moscovici said on Tuesday that Paris needed more than a week to study the pact and carry out an audit of state finances.

German shares got off to a rocky start in bourse trade, falling slightly in volatile trade due to worries about the single European currency and the future of the ruling Bonn coalition. But the 30-share DAX index was up 1.52 points at 3,668.95 by 1130 GMT.

In London, Britain's FTSE 100 bounced to the day's best level in late morning trading, but investors seemed increasingly reluctant to push the index above the 4,700 mark, dealers said. By 1130 GMT, it stood at 4,697.2.
"It's quite a key resistance level and every time we get near 4,700, we see a bit of stock for sale," one dealer said.
He said he expected to see increased volatility in the market in the days leading up to July 2, when the new government will publish its first budget.

While weakness in German and French bourses was keeping investors jittery, problems facing EMU had given British shares a boost recently as investors shift into British assets because of their perceived safety. Dealers said the uncertainty surrounding the project may soon bleed into British financial markets.
"Markets will come to terms with any situation: no matter how bearish, it can be priced in. But you can't value uncertainty," one dealer said. "There's nothing markets hate more than uncertainty."
In currencies, the dollar clawed back above 1.71 marks, but struggled to extend its rebound amid lingering concern EMU may be delayed.

"Since the stability pact represents the very essence of the philosophical differences between France and Germany over macro-economic policy it is difficult to envisage an easy, painless fix," said Paul Meggyesi, senior currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.

Short-covering and assurances from European Union officials that the French request will not delay the launch of the European single currency lifted the dollar from the one-week low it set against the mark Monday. Still, traders expected it to hold below 1.72 marks until France reveals its stance on the pact.

"A great deal was made of the French announcement in London, but there is a somewhat different attitude towards it in Europe," said Keith Lewis, the manager of treasury markets at American Express Bank.
"While worries about EMU persist, (dollar/mark) will remain in a 1.69 to 1.72 range, but so much still favours the dollar that this is being viewed as a trading opportunity."
The dollar was steady against the yen at around 112.40 before the release of Japanese current account data.
CURRENCIES AT 1130 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7120 marks and 112.40 yen compared with 1.7063 marks and 112.55 yen on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1130 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 10.5 points at 4,697.2.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 19.47 points at 2,666.73.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 1.52 points at 3,668.95.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1130 GMT
Gold fixed at $344.00 compared with Monday's close of $344.25.
